summary: This program picks a game level name from a number using the ternary operator, a compact one-expression alternative to an if/else chain, and prints the result.

lines.code: int levelNumber = 17; // change this value to test
lines.text: The single number that drives the whole decision; edit it and re-run to see each branch fire in turn.
A ternary is an expression that produces a value, so it can sit directly on the right of an assignment: the condition before the ? is tested, and the value after it is used when the test is true.

The part after the colon is the "otherwise" value, and here it is another ternary. Chaining this way is how a ternary handles more than two outcomes, and because we only reach it when levelNumber is not below 10, the test needs no lower bound.
Every ternary must supply a final else value, so this last branch has no condition and catches anything 20 or above. The semicolon ends the assignment statement that began three lines earlier.
The decision was already made when level was assigned, so printing is a separate, trivial step; keeping the choice and the output apart lets you reuse level elsewhere.
